Bledow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Błędów, Poland

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Błędów in the second half of the 19th century; Rabbi Jakow Icchak Szapiro, son of the Mogielnica Rebbe, once lived there. By 1921, 815 Jews made up over 43% of the village's population, and were deported to the Warsaw Ghetto in February 1941. The cemetery, likely established in the 19th century, suffered extensive destruction - local residents used its tombstones for construction and grinding wheels, and Communist-era authorities operated a gravel mine and later a shooting range there. A 1985 survey found nothing recognizable as a cemetery, just a meadow doubling as a garbage dump. In 1996, a local veterinarian and two collaborators from Denmark (including Rabbi Tom Trier) founded a restoration committee that fenced part of the site and installed a Star-of-David gateway; dozens of recovered matzevot were added in 1998 and a menorah monument erected. Vandals destroyed the monument and part of the fence in 2004, but the commune office now maintains the site regularly.
